headline: 30 resolved trades, net -1.04 bps/bet (-31.3 total); rolling 17-bet gross -2.39 bps. Signal flat at 0.
regime_note: BTC ~$84.7k, still consolidating well above the mid-August low-$60ks after the late-August step-up; choppy, high-variance tape. Signal is 0, so no live position right now.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing.** Little has changed since last check. The full live ledger still shows 30 resolved trades averaging **-1.04 bps/bet** (total **-31.3 bps**), with a **40% win rate**. The rolling 17-bet window is weaker: **-2.39 bps gross**, **-5.39 bps net** at an assumed 3.0 bps cost. The signal is currently **0**, so nothing is live right now.

**What changed vs last time.** Essentially nothing — same trade count, same aggregate numbers, same flat signal. No new resolved trades have shifted the picture.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us.** They *do* confirm this edge is marginal, exactly as the research warned: gross edge ~4 bps against a ~3.9 bps breakeven. They *don't* prove the strategy is broken. 30 trades (17 in the rolling window) is a tiny, high-variance sample — note individual trades swing from -28 to +52 bps. A handful of large losers (the -25 and -13 bps shorts) dominate the mean. At this sample size, a run of modestly negative results is fully consistent with either a flat/zero edge or ordinary noise around breakeven.

**Bottom line.** Live results are mildly negative but statistically inconclusive, and squarely in line with the pre-registered 'likely not net-profitable after costs' expectation. That the broader edge search found **0 survivors** at 5 bps cost reinforces caution. No action warranted on noise — but do not expect this to be a money-maker. Keep logging; revisit once the sample is materially larger.
